title: Capsule Protocol Policy and Registry Architecture
purpose: Define RFC 9297 Capsule Protocol response/header policy, HTTP/3 CONNECT restrictions, no-content constraints, Capsule-Protocol structured-field handling, and Capsule Type registry invariants.
design_summary: `Http3CapsuleProtocol` keeps Capsule Protocol policy separate from stream and proxy runtime behavior. It validates that HTTP/3 Capsule Protocol use is attached to CONNECT, allows only 101 or valid 2xx statuses while excluding 204/205/206, rejects HTTP content headers or body bytes, parses Capsule-Protocol as an Item Structured Field Boolean, treats false or non-Boolean values as absent, ignores unknown parameters, exposes the registered field name, and models Capsule Type registry reservation and assignment policy.
data_and_state_considerations: The policy is pure and stateless. It does not parse live stream bytes, buffer capsules, open tunnels, emit datagrams, or mutate request/response objects.
edge_cases_and_constraints: False and non-Boolean Capsule-Protocol values are absence-equivalent.
Unknown Capsule-Protocol parameters do not affect the true/false Boolean item.
Status 101 and successful statuses are allowed except 204, 205, and 206.
Content-Length, Content-Type, Transfer-Encoding, and nonzero content byte counts make Capsule Protocol use malformed.
Capsule Type values of the form 0x29 * N + 0x17 are reserved and not assignable.
risks: Runtime stream lifecycle and QUIC DATAGRAM send/receive behavior remain out of scope.
Type-specific Capsule payload field validation remains out of scope.
CONNECT-UDP and CONNECT-IP request semantics remain in RFC 9298 and RFC 9484 slices.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This policy slice lets later MASQUE adapters ask whether a request/response pair is allowed to use Capsule Protocol without coupling policy checks to proxy forwarding or QUIC transport state.
